title: Exponential XOR hardness amplification through random simplification

standard_prerequisites.name: Decision trees, conditional expectation and product distributions
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Author Definitions 2.1, 2.4, 2.5; necessary definitions and full author Claim3.3 retained.

core_obligations: Retain the author approximate-uniformity decomposition and complete supporting max-divergence argument.
Apply the complete robust decision-tree XOR result to surviving independent blocks.
Combine the exponential simplification tail and block-selection probabilities to obtain the amplified correlation bound.
difficulty_reason: The author uses an approximate completion to uniform inputs, a random surviving-block decomposition, robust decision-tree XOR amplification and an exponential simplification tail. Their combination removes the additive failure term of the simpler framework and is a nonroutine general amplification result.

dedup.scope: Full reference snapshots have zero hits for source DOI, ECCC alias, journal DOI and title. The target is the random-simplification transfer theorem Lemma4.2, distinct from standalone decision-tree XOR Lemma3.2: it introduces generalized restrictions, approximate completion of the uniform distribution and exponential simplification tails. Lemma3.2 is included with complete proof as uncounted support in this item; no claims3.3/3.6/lemma2.3 are counted.

compared.difference: Standalone correlation amplification for decision trees versus transfer of hardness amplification to general restriction-closed Boolean classes through random simplification.
